prose: An Instacloud blog post argues that a million agents is a distributed system problem: one agent is a worker, a thousand agents is an organization, and an organization of machines is a distributed system. It cites recent research warnings: unrestricted access to LLM or tool resources can lead to inefficient or harmful allocation; the 'more agents' approach hits a ceiling and can degrade performance; and agents spontaneously form coordination topologies yet systematically fail to synthesize distributed state into correct answers.

The author's frame: agents can technically run forever, but they run on finite stuff - tokens, context, compute, memory, tools, money. Humans cope the same way: we write the important parts down, sleep, and come back with a clear head.
highlights: Thesis: a million agents is an organization, i.e. a distributed system.
Cites research: unrestricted resource access leads to inefficient or harmful allocation.
'More agents' hits a ceiling and can degrade performance.
Agents form coordination topologies but fail to synthesize distributed state into correct answers.
Agents run on finite tokens, context, compute, memory, tools and money.
